#!/bin/bash
# Deploy a ref (default: main from /opt/nxeon) to the staging environment.
# Usage: ./scripts/deploy-staging.sh [git-ref]
set -euo pipefail
REF="${1:-main}"
cd /opt/nxeon-staging
echo "==> Syncing staging to $REF"
git fetch origin
git reset --hard "origin/$REF"
echo "==> Installing dependencies"
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -1
echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss 2>&1 | tail -2
npm run db:seed 2>&1 | tail -2 || true
echo "==> Building"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4
# next.config sets output:"standalone" but the systemd unit runs the standalone
# server.js directly (not `next start`, which Next.js explicitly does not
# support alongside output:"standalone" — it prints a warning and silently
# fails to resolve some routes, confirmed live 2026-09-10: a brand-new API
# route 404'd under `next start` on this exact build and returned 200 under
# `node .next/standalone/server.js`). The standalone output does NOT include
# public/ or .next/static/ (Next's own documented behavior) — copy them in
# fresh every build, or every static asset/route added after the last copy
# is missing until the next deploy happens to also touch this step.
echo "==> Copying static assets into the standalone server output"
rm -rf .next/standalone/public .next/standalone/.next/static
cp -r public .next/standalone/public
cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static
# geoip-lite is in next.config.ts's serverExternalPackages (kept OUT of the JS
# bundle on purpose, since it reads .dat files off its own package path at
# runtime) — but the standalone output tracer only copies files it can trace
# as JS-imported, so an externalized package's own non-JS data files are
# silently left behind. Found live 2026-09-10: this crashed EVERY request
# with an uncaught ENOENT the moment the systemd unit ran the standalone

## VPS RAM ticket (黃聖威, web-01-pvm4): fixed live on node-4, code fix on staging, reply drafted but not sent

**Result:** the customer's VM now has its full 8 GB. Inside the guest `free -h` shows **7.8Gi** (it was 3.8Gi), and I checked it again about 20 minutes later. Nothing was rebooted. Eight other paying VMs on node-4 had the same problem and are fixed too. The code fix is on staging and waits for you to promote it. Until you do, prod keeps giving every new VPS or resize the 50% floor.

### Root cause
It's ballooning. Provisioning and resize were both fine.
- **Server row:** `cmuevsfqn0s6uhl7a5u3vistu`, VMID 133 on node-4 (ns564103), plan `pro` (3 vCPU / 8192 MB / 80 GB), created 2026-09-24. It has no upgrades or resizes. Job history is PROVISION, REINSTALL, 3 REBOOTs and firewall/forward syncs.
- **Proxmox config:** `memory: 8192`, `balloon: 4096`. `qm status --verbose` showed `actual 4096 MB`, `max_mem 8192`, and the guest had about 554 MB swapped out.
- **Where the 4096 came from:** commit `1271914cf0` (2026-09-14) added `balloonFloorMB = max(1024, memory × 0.5)` to `worker/index.ts`. PROVISION and RESIZE both use it.
- **Why it bites:** Proxmox (pvestatd) shrinks every ballooned VM down to its floor whenever the host is above 80% RAM used. Node-4's RRD history shows the host crossing 80% around 2026-09-24 14:00 UTC, about 12 hours after this VM was built, and staying there. So from then until today the VM was held at exactly half its plan.
- **What made it possible:** `lib/capacity.ts` sells RAM at 1.5× each node's `capacityRamMB` by default. The design only worked by squeezing customers.
- `onboard-node.sh` doesn't set any balloon value, so it isn't involved.

### What I changed live on node-4
For each VM I ran `qm set <id> --balloon <plan MB>` and then `echo "balloon <plan MB>" | qm monitor <id>`. The second command is needed because pvestatd won't grow a VM while the host is above 80%.

Before → after, as reported by `free -m` in the guest via the guest agent:

| VMID | Server | Plan RAM | Guest total before | Guest total after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **133** | web-01-pvm4 (this customer) | 8 GB | 3845 MB | **7941 MB** |
| 130 | web-01-oyrj (ammadshaikh63) | 8 GB | 3845 MB | 7941 MB |
| 128 | cs2 | 4 GB | 1867 MB | 3915 MB |
| 132 | minecraft | 4 GB | 1867 MB (97 MB available, 1.1 GB in swap) | 3915 MB |
| 136 | rust | 4 GB | 1867 MB | 3915 MB (immediately used about 3.9 GB) |
| 131 | upnormal | 2 GB | 943 MB | 1967 MB |
| 134 | corekeeper | 2 GB | 943 MB (1.8 GB in swap) | 1967 MB |
| 135 | minecraft | 2 GB | 943 MB | 1967 MB |
| 137 | vps-v87z | 2 GB | 943 MB | 1967 MB |

**Node-4 host numbers:** 64084 MB total. Before: 54247 used, 9396 free, ZFS cache (ARC) at its 8 GB max. After: 53427 used, 10220 free, 10656 available. Most of these VMs' host memory was never actually released while they were squeezed, so restoring them cost almost nothing. If every guest filled all of its RAM, the host would need about 6.3 GB more, which fits in what's free plus what the ZFS cache can give back. Every VM with a Server row on node-4 now has a floor equal to its plan, so pvestatd has nothing left to squeeze.

### Fleet-wide: VMs with a floor below their plan (read-only)
- **node-3: all 7 paying VMs are squeezed, and I did not fix them.** VMIDs 107, 122, 125, 126 (4 GB plans, getting 2 GB), 119 terraheim and 500 darkeden (8 GB, getting 4 GB), and 127 shizu-valheim (floor 4096, but actually getting 3148 MB).
  - The node is sold past its hardware: 36,864 MB of plans on a 31,862 MB host, with only about 3.8 GB free and the ZFS cache allowed to reach 8 GB.
  - Restoring everyone needs about 14 GB. The fix is to move VMs off node-3 (node-2 has about 16 GB available), which means downtime you'd schedule with each customer. Capping the ZFS cache would help a little.
- **primary: 6 paying VMs are partly squeezed, and I did not fix them.** 109 (1836 of 2048 MB), 111 (2455/4096), 112 (1636/2048), 116 (2580/4096), 120 blue (4951/8192), 121 projectzomboid (4096/6144). Your own 105 is also squeezed (4815/8192).
  - Restoring them could need about 14.9 GB against 16.4 GB available. That leaves no margin on the box that runs the web app, Postgres and builds, and it had an out-of-memory crash on 09-14.
  - Once headroom exists, it's the same two commands per VM.
- **node-2: at risk, but not squeezed today** (host is at about 74%). 103, 123, 124 and 139 are paid VMs with 50% floors; 100 and 129 are free VMs with the same. Running the same `qm set --balloon <mem>` there costs nothing, but I didn't do it because they aren't affected right now.
- **VMs with no matching Server row (reported, not touched):**
  - node-2 **101 sausaugepro**: running and using 8 GB. The DB row for sausaugepro is VMID 600 on node-4, so this looks like a leftover copy.
  - node-2 116, 117, 137, 138: stopped leftovers.
  - node-4 501 nxlabs-storage: floor 2048, squeezed to it.
  - primary 114 (stopped), 200 hosting-1, 8000 nxeon-mail.
- **Other mismatches between the DB and Proxmox:**
  - primary 110 kodely-app is on the 1 GB `nano` plan but configured with 6144 MB.
  - primary 118 dst is entitled to 3072 MB but configured with 6144 MB (over-delivered, not a customer problem).
  - primary 106 and 110 are STOPPED in the DB but running in Proxmox.
  - node-2 139 is ERROR in the DB but running.

### Code fix: on staging, waiting for you to promote
- Branch `fix/vps-ram-allocation`, commit `43ad6f772f`, pushed, worktree at `/root/nxeon-worktrees/vps-ram`.
- `worker/index.ts`: `balloonFloorMB()` now returns the full `memory`. The balloon device stays, so a floor can still be changed on a running VM.
- `lib/capacity.ts`: the default `RAM_OVERSELL_FACTOR` is now 1.0 instead of 1.5. Without the squeeze, oversold RAM would mean out-of-memory crashes. Node-2 and node-4 each still have about 11 GB of room, so sales aren't blocked.
- `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`: capacity section updated and a dated change-history entry added.
- `tsc --noEmit` is clean and the capacity tests pass (9/9). I did not provision a real VM on staging.
- Staging deployed and returns HTTP 200. The first build attempt failed on a Google Fonts fetch; the retry was clean.
- **Staging was running another session's commit** (`af0d5f9a`, branch promo-trial-798) and my deploy replaced it. There were no schema or package differences, so the staging DB wasn't affected. That session may need to redeploy its branch.
- **Decision for you:** node-4's `capacityRamMB` is 56000. Real sellable RAM is about 52900 (64084 minus the 8 GB ZFS cache minus about 3 GB for the host). Either lower it to about 52000 or cap the ZFS cache at 4 GB.

### Credit
The SLA (`lib/legal/sla.ts`) only covers uptime, so it doesn't formally apply. The customer paid $20.99 for the month and had half the RAM from about 24 Sep 14:00 UTC to 28 Sep 02:05 UTC (about 3.5 days). A prorated amount is about $1.25. A goodwill credit (for example $5, or 25% of the month) seems deserved. Your call. The other eight node-4 customers were squeezed over the same window, and most haven't noticed.

### Draft reply (NOT sent)
The earlier "Nxeon Admin" reply said "From our front end we also see 8GB so that is very odd, let me investigate the matter." This follows on from it:

> Hi,
>
> Thanks for reporting this, and for including your `free -h` output. It made the cause quick to find.
>
> You were right. Your server was set up with 8 GB, but a memory-sharing setting on our side let the system hold back up to half of a server's RAM when the machine it runs on got busy. That happened to yours from about 24 September, so it was limited to roughly 4 GB. This was our mistake, not anything in your setup.
>
> We've fixed it without restarting your server. `free -h` should now show about 7.8Gi total; the small gap from 8 GB is memory the Linux kernel keeps for itself, which is normal. We've also changed the setting so your server can't be limited like this again, and it won't happen to new servers either.
>
> [Optional: As an apology, we've added $X credit to your account balance.]
>
> If you see anything other than about 7.8Gi, just reply here and we'll look into it right away.
>
> — The Nxeon team
